Annotate ATAC peaks with nearest genomic features

Source: R/AnnotateATACPeaks.R
AnnotateATACPeaks.Rd

Attach verified gene annotation and record native nearest-feature distances, retaining native nearest-feature hits and unmatched peaks.

Usage

AnnotateATACPeaks(object, annotation, assay = NULL, verbose = TRUE)

Arguments

object

A Seurat object with a validated ChromatinAssay.

annotation

A non-empty Signac-compatible GRanges of 1-based closed gene/transcript intervals with gene_id, gene_name, gene_biotype, type and tx_id (or transcript_id) metadata. It must declare the source assay's genome label. Known chromosome lengths must agree and interval ends must not exceed them. Extra chromosomes are retained without name conversion.

assay

Source chromatin assay; defaults to the active assay.

verbose

Whether to print progress messages.

Value

The Seurat object with native Signac gene annotation and Misc(object[[assay]], "scop_peak_annotation"). The receipt contains nearest, an S4Vectors::DataFrame with peak ID, annotation row index, distance and prefixed annotation metadata; unannotated_peaks lists peaks without a hit. Rows follow peak order and annotation index within ties. Counts, cells, other assays and reductions are unchanged.

Details

Nearest distances are computed by GenomicRanges::distanceToNearest(select = "all", ignore.strand = TRUE). Distance counts the bases between intervals; overlaps and adjacent intervals have distance zero. These are distances to annotation intervals, not to TSSs, promoter classifications, regulatory links, or evidence of gene regulation. Different transcripts can produce several native hits. select = "all" does not guarantee every mathematical tie on both sides of a peak: native GenomicRanges tie selection is preserved. No genome download or chromosome-style conversion is performed. Existing annotation must be identical after native Signac normalization (including transcript_id to tx_id); existing results are not replaced. Genome labels and known lengths are checked, not reference sequence contents. Nonmatching chromosome names remain unmatched rather than being translated.

See also

FilterATACPeaks(), CheckATACData()

Examples

counts <- Matrix::sparseMatrix(
  i = c(1, 2, 1), j = c(1, 2, 2), x = c(2, 3, 1), dims = c(2, 2),
  dimnames = list(c("p1", "p2"), c("cell1", "cell2"))
)
ranges <- GenomicRanges::GRanges(c("chr1:1-50", "chr1:101-150"))
object <- ReadATACData(counts, ranges = ranges, genome = "hg38")
annotation <- GenomicRanges::GRanges("chr1:1-80")
GenomeInfoDb::genome(annotation) <- "hg38"
S4Vectors::mcols(annotation) <- S4Vectors::DataFrame(
  gene_id = "gene1", gene_name = "GENE1", gene_biotype = "protein_coding",
  type = "gene", tx_id = "tx1"
)
object <- AnnotateATACPeaks(object, annotation, verbose = FALSE)
SeuratObject::Misc(object[["peaks"]], "scop_peak_annotation")$nearest
#> DataFrame with 2 rows and 8 columns
#>           peak annotation_index  distance annotation_gene_id
#>    <character>        <integer> <integer>        <character>
#> 1    chr1-1-50                1         0              gene1
#> 2 chr1-101-150                1        20              gene1
#>   annotation_gene_name annotation_gene_biotype annotation_type annotation_tx_id
#>            <character>             <character>     <character>      <character>
#> 1                GENE1          protein_coding            gene              tx1
#> 2                GENE1          protein_coding            gene              tx1
